problems.title: Differentiate a sum using chain and product rules
problems.question: Differentiate $y=\tan\sqrt x-(x+2)e^{2x}+\ln(4x)+\arctan(2x+1)$.
problems.idea: Differentiate each term and include every inner derivative.
steps: The first derivative term is 1/[2√x cos²√x].
The product derivative is −[e²ˣ+2(x+2)e²ˣ]=−(2x+5)e²ˣ.
The logarithm derivative is 4/(4x)=1/x. The arctangent derivative is 2/[1+(2x+1)²].

problems.title: A rhombus rotated around a side
problems.question: A rhombus of side 6 cm and acute angle 60° rotates about one side. Find the solid’s volume and surface area.
problems.idea: The top side creates a cylindrical surface, and the two slanted sides create conical surfaces.
formulas: Altitude r=6sin60°=3√3; rhombus area=18√3; centroid distance to axis=r/2.
steps: Volume=area×2π·centroid distance=18√3·2π·(3√3/2)=162π.
The opposite side creates a cylinder of length 6 and radius 3√3, with lateral area 2π·3√3·6=36√3π.
Each slanted side creates a cone surface of slant length 6 and radius 3√3, area 18√3π. One is the exterior end and the other bounds the end cavity.
Add both cone surfaces and the cylinder surface.

problems.title: Three sequence limits
problems.question: Find (a) $\lim(\sqrt{n^2-n}-n)$; (b) $\lim((n+1)/n)^{5n+2}$; (c) $\lim[\sum_{k=1}^n k\,k!]/(n+1)!$, as $n\to\infty$.
problems.idea: Use rationalization, the definition of e, and a telescoping factorial sum.
steps: (a) The rationalized denominator tends to 2, so the limit is −1/2.
(b) Write the expression as [(1+1/n)ⁿ]⁵(1+1/n)²; the limit is e⁵.
(c) The numerator telescopes to (n+1)!−1, so the quotient tends to 1.

problems.title: A bounded sine limit and a zero-over-zero limit
problems.question: Find (a) $\lim_{x\to\infty}(1-\sqrt x-x)\sin(x+\pi/3)/(x^2+2)$; (b) $\lim_{x\to\pi/3}\sin(x-\pi/3)/(1-2\cos x)$.
problems.idea: Bound the sine in the first limit; compare first derivatives in the second.
formulas: |sin t|≤1; for (b), numerator derivative=cos(x−π/3), denominator derivative=2sin x.
steps: (a) The absolute value is at most (1+√x+x)/(x²+2), which tends to 0.
(b) Both functions vanish at π/3 and are differentiable there, with denominator derivative √3≠0. Their ratio tends to 1/√3.

problems.title: Discontinuities of an absolute-value quotient
problems.question: Find the discontinuity points of f(x)=x/[x|x−3|−|x|].
problems.idea: Solve the denominator equation separately for negative and positive x.
steps: x=0 is excluded. The left limit there is 1/4 and the right limit 1/2, so it is a jump discontinuity.
For x>0, the denominator vanishes at |x−3|=1, giving x=2,4; both are vertical asymptotes.
At x=3 the absolute-value formula changes, but the denominator is nonzero and the function remains continuous.

problems.title: Two tangents from a point below a parabola
problems.question: Two tangents to f(x)=x²−2x−3 pass through M=(−1,−9). Find the acute angle between them.
problems.idea: Write the tangent at input t and require it to pass through M.
steps: Thus t=2 or −4; the slopes are 2 and −10.
The acute-angle formula gives tanθ=|[2−(−10)]/[1+2(−10)]|=12/19.

problems.title: All roots of a parameter log equation must lie below 3
problems.question: Find a such that (a−1)[log₃(x−2)]²−2(a+1)log₃(x−2)+a−3=0 has real roots, all less than 3.
problems.idea: Set t=log₃(x−2). The condition 2<x<3 becomes t<0.
formulas: For a≠1: D=8(3a−1), root sum=2(a+1)/(a−1), product=(a−3)/(a−1).
steps: Real roots require a≥1/3. Both t-roots negative require negative sum and positive product, which together give a<1 in this range.
Hence 1/3≤a<1 works, including the negative double root at a=1/3.
At a=1 the equation is linear: −4t−2=0, so t=−1/2<0 and it also works.

problems.title: A conical frustum with ambiguous diagonal-angle wording
problems.question: The axial-section diagonals of a cone frustum have length 3 m, split each other 2:1, and make a stated angle of 120°. Find volume and lateral area.
problems.idea: The diagonal split fixes R:r=2:1. But two intersecting lines have both supplementary angles unless a sector is specified.
formulas: Let s=R+r. Then s²+h²=9; V=πh(R²+Rr+r²)/3; lateral area=π(R+r)√[h²+(R−r)²].
steps: If the angle between the rays to the lower-base endpoints is 120°, then s/h=√3. Thus h=3/2,s=3√3/2, r=√3/2,R=√3.
This gives V=21π/8 m³ and lateral area=9π/2 m².
If the indicated 120° is the left/right angle instead, h/s=√3. Then h=3√3/2,s=3/2,r=1/2,R=1.
That case gives V=7√3π/8 m³ and lateral area=3√7π/2 m².
problems.answer: First placement: V=21π/8, lateral area=9π/2. Other placement: V=7√3π/8, lateral area=3√7π/2.
problems.note: No diagram or specified sector selects which 120° intersection angle is meant. Both sets satisfy the printed diagonal conditions.

problems.title: The gap from a line to a circle
problems.question: A lies on 3x−4y=−34 and B on x²+y²−8x+2y=8. Find the minimum AB.
problems.idea: Find the circle centre and compare its radius with the centre-to-line distance.
steps: The centre-to-line distance is 50/5=10, and the radius is 5.
The closest points lie along the perpendicular from the centre to the line, so the gap is 10−5.

problems.title: A cone net angle from an inscribed sphere
problems.question: A sphere inscribed in a cone has surface area 36π. The cone height is 8. Find the central angle of its lateral net.
problems.idea: Recover the sphere radius and use the axial triangle’s inradius.
steps: ρ=3, so 3(R+l)=8R, giving l=5R/3.
The net angle is 360°·6/10.
